descript.abstract: This data release and model archive contains geochemical and microbial reaction modeling input files, selected output files, and an accompanying data dictionary. The files were used to simulate hydrogen consumption during underground hydrogen storage (UHS). Batch-reaction simulations were developed using the React program in Geochemist’s Workbench (GWB) and are based on estimated formation-water chemistry from the Mississippian Aux Vases Formation in the Illinois Basin. The models represent coupled geochemical and microbial processes in a closed porous system, including microbial sulfate reduction and hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis, reaction kinetics, biomass growth, and feedbacks with pH and temperature, and were run over short- and long-term timescales.
descript.purpose: The simulations were developed to evaluate the potential impacts of microbial sulfate reduction and hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis on hydrogen stability during underground hydrogen storage in a depleted hydrocarbon reservoir. Estimated water chemistry data from Mississippian Aux Vases Formation of the Illinois Basin (Demir and Seyler, 1999) was used as initial input.
descript.supplinf: One or more files contain data available in comma separated value (.csv) file format. The user must have software capable of opening and viewing a .csv file. It is recommended that data users consult the manuscript associated with this data release (crossref) for a detailed description of the methods, model input and assumptions. The simulations were developed using Geochemist’s Workbench (GWB) Professional, which is commercially available and requires a paid license for use. While the input files provided in this data release are complete, reproduction of the simulations requires access to a licensed copy of the software. srcinfo.srccontr: Estimated water chemistry for a Mississippian Aux Vases reservoir in the Illinois Basin

procstep.procdesc: The batch reaction simulations performed in this study used the React program of the Geochemist’s Workbench (GWB) version 17.0 as the modeling tool. Water chemistry from a single well (EOR-B106) in the Mississippian Aux Vases Formation in the Illinois Basin was used to model microbial reactions triggered by hydrogen in a closed system under reservoir conditions. For complete reference list and method description, please see the manuscript associated with this data release (crossref).

Thermodynamic and kinetic data for microbial sulfate reduction and hydrogenotrohpic methanogenesis were sourced from the literature. Parameters were originally acquired from laboratory experiments or modeling experiments replicating real world conditions. Simulations were performed for long term (12,700 years) and short term (365 days) time frames. Furthermore, the influence of pH and temperature on reaction rate and hydrogen loss were assessed by varying these parameters independently. For complete reference list and method description, please see the manuscript associated with this data release (crossref).

To evaluate the sensitivity of model output to input data uncertainties, a series of simulations were conducted. The parameters tested include initial biomass concentration and rate constant for sulfate reduction and hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis, initial sulfate and bicarbonate concentrations, and initial salinity expressed as total dissolved solids (TDS). These parameters were independently varied above and below the baseline values used in this model. The time frame for these simulations was arbitrarily set to run for 50 years.
